title: 🔥 The Roast: Week 11
preview: The Commish lost to the quarterback he cut, Drew benched a week-high, Brad took his revenge five points at a time, and Mike ate what the other tables sent back. Tap if you can take it.
schedule_note: New roasts drop every Wednesday at 6 PM ET, right after waivers and before Thursday night.
intro: Week 10 gave us the biggest blowout of the dynasty era, a 50-point running back, a commissioner beaten by his own garbage, and a man who benched 48 points and blamed nobody. Somebody in this league had a clean week. It wasn't any of you. Week 11 kicks off Thursday. Nobody is safe.
facts_note: Every fact is real: Sleeper Week 10 results and lineups, transactions through Wednesday Nov 18, Week 11 matchups, and AP/NFL.com game reports. Streaks are head-to-head only. A roast among friends.

entries.roast: Ladies and gentlemen... in the blue corner... weighing in at sixteen wins, three losses and one tie... the undisputed regular-season champion of absolutely nothing... TheBELT-LESSSSS! Let's get ready to rumbleeee! Maddox dropped 207.6. Gibbs went for 48.7, Dak threw five touchdowns, and the crowd went home happy. But even the champ can't stop flinching: Josh Downs sat on his bench and outscored Malik Nabers by nearly eight points. You can win every round, Jacob, and still leave a punch on the stool. Sixteen wins. Best record in the league by two and a half games. And every week he walks to the ring in a robe that says, in giant letters, that he doesn't have the belt. You named yourself after the one thing you can't win, champ. Nobody else had to.
entries.this_week: vs Taylor Alvarado: 16-3-1 on a one-game win streak, against 4-16 and five straight losses. The main event is a man with no belt against a man with no pulse.
entries.prediction: Maddox wins by 50, and the robe still says Belt-Less.

entries.roast: Dear Abby: Tuesday, I broke up with my quarterback. Drew Lock. I'm the Commissioner, I have standards, and I left him on the curb for a more exciting receiver named Ryan Flournoy. Two days later, Lock is living at Mike's house. Sunday, Mike brings him to MY game, and he throws two touchdowns against me. He fumbles twice, once by running into his own running back, and it still doesn't matter. Meanwhile my new man, Flournoy, scores 19.1 sitting on my couch while I start Chris Olave for 6.0. I lost by 50. Abby, what do I do? Signed, THE Dictator. Dear Dictator: You dumped a guy, didn't even play the one you left him for, and then watched your ex beat you while running into his own teammate. That's not heartbreak, sweetie. That's a waiver claim with a restraining order. Lose Mike's number.
entries.this_week: vs Brian Mulvihill: 9-11 with a one-game skid, against 14-6 on a two-game win streak. Brian just picked up a tight end for this, and the Commish is still trying to figure out which receiver to start.
entries.prediction: Brian wins by 12, and the Commish benches the guy who would have won it.

entries.roast: Bradley. Okay. So. Let's talk about the implication. Week 1, Taylor hung 232.5 on you and won by 79.4. You waited nine weeks. You stewed. And Sunday you got your revenge: Mahomes throws five touchdowns, a rookie named Emmett Johnson drops 37.1 out of your flex, and you beat Taylor by 84.6, the biggest blowout of the dynasty era. Which puts you, after ten weeks of plotting, exactly 5.2 points ahead of the worst team in the league. Five points! That's your revenge arc. A whole season of hatred for a field goal and a safety. And even after the week-high, you're still under .500, at 9-10-1, level in wins with the Commish, Drew and Kyle, plus a tie. The implication is you're dangerous, Brad. Nobody in this league is in any danger.
entries.this_week: vs Kyle Llano: 9-10-1 on a two-game win streak, against 9-11 and two straight losses. Brad can get back to .500, Kyle can get back to one under, and both will call it a playoff push.
entries.prediction: Brad wins by 9 and celebrates like it was 84.

entries.roast: Brian won, so he'd like you to know he's 14-6. Here's how. He put up 131.3, the fourth-lowest score in the league, beat the lowest score of the week, and lost to the median. Sixty percent of the league outscored him and he got a W for it. Thursday he grabs Darren Waller and slides him straight into the flex. 4.4 points, with Malik Washington's 13.7 sitting on the bench. Same day he adds Carson Beck. Beck makes his first NFL start Sunday, Arizona loses 34-6, and Beck scores -2.0 on Brian's bench. Brian spent a waiver claim on a quarterback who lost him points without ever leaving the bench. That's not a contender. That's a guy who wins at bingo and asks for a ring. Today he flipped Rome Odunze to Drew for Sam LaPorta, a tight end who scored 2.6 for Drew last week. One more tight end and Brian can start a Waller-LaPorta flex and lose to the median on purpose.
entries.this_week: vs Ryan Nussdorfer: 14-6 on a two-game win streak, against 9-11 with a one-game skid. Brian gets the Commish the week after Mike already showed everyone how.
entries.prediction: Brian wins by 12 with the fourth-lowest score again.

entries.roast: Gronk Nation, I'm gonna need you to stay calm. Saturday, Michigan went to Oregon and lost 31-7. Five drives in the second half, five turnovers. Oregon didn't need a defense. They needed a lost-and-found. Kyle, Michigan lives rent-free in your head, and they're behind on the rent. Then Sunday, it's your turn. Tuesday you claim Corey Kiner off waivers, and Sunday you start him. 2.5 points. Kaelon Black scored 13.6 on your bench. You start Evan McPherson for 7.0 and bench Cameron Dicker for 11.0. Two coin-flip calls, two wrong sides, 15 points in the trash. Two straight losses, 9-11, and the one team you love just turned it over every time it touched the ball after halftime. At least you came by it honestly, Kyle. It runs in the fanbase.
entries.this_week: vs Bradley Kochheiser: 9-11 and two straight losses, against 9-10-1 on a two-game win streak. Kyle's playing the hottest team in the league that's still under .500.
entries.prediction: Brad wins by 9, and Kyle starts the kicker who doesn't score.

entries.roast: Are YOU tired of winning by too much? Do you hate leaving points on the table... unless they're 20-point defenses? Introducing Bed, Bath, and Bijan! For just three easy payments of 40.75 from Joe Burrow and 32.3 from Trevor Lawrence, you get a 24-point win AND the Rams defense, 20.45 points, sitting on the bench in the original packaging! He started Seattle's instead. But wait, there's more! Act now and he'll throw in Javonte Williams in the starting lineup with Aaron Jones scoring nearly double on the bench! Two straight wins! Alone in fourth at 11-9! And the power rankings still have him sixth, behind a 9-11 Kyle. That's right. Fourth-best record in the league, and the experts looked at it and said, results not typical. Operators are standing by. Nobody's calling.
entries.this_week: vs Nick Cardillo: 11-9 on a two-game win streak, against 6-14 with a one-game skid. Kasik gets a Coastal Elite who's spending the week looking for a quarterback.
entries.prediction: Kasik wins by 20 and leaves the better defense on the bench again.

entries.roast: The prosecution calls Chase Brown. Mr. Brown, where were you Sunday night? "Catching two touchdowns. 28.3 points." And where was Mr. Hartman's lineup? "Starting DeMario Douglas." The witness may step down. The prosecution calls DeMario Douglas. Mr. Douglas, when did the defendant acquire you? "Tuesday." And what did you score? "1.4." And where are you now? "He cut me this afternoon." No further questions. Ladies and gentlemen of the jury: start Brown, start DJ Moore over Jalen Coker's 0.3, and Drew Hartman scores 210.25. That beats Maddox. That beats everybody but Brad. Instead he lost by 44. Jordan Belfort's Nuts had the week's second-best team, and he left it on the bench. The defense rests. So did Chase Brown.
entries.this_week: vs Mike Hemstreet: 9-11 and two straight losses, against 12-8 on a one-game win streak. Drew traded for Rome Odunze today, so this week he has a brand new receiver to sit.
entries.prediction: Mike wins by 15, and Drew's best lineup finishes second on the bench again.

entries.roast: Oh, darling. The Coastal Elites. Such a lovely name for the lowest score in the league. George Pickens put up 45.5 on Sunday. Eleven catches, three touchdowns. And Cardillo still lost, because the other nine starters scraped together 74.85 between them. One man hosted the dinner party, and everyone else showed up with a bag of ice. His quarterback gave him 3.0 points. Now his quarterback room is Michael Penix and a questionable Baker Mayfield, which is less of a room and more of a closet. 6-14, eighth in the power rankings, ahead of only Taylor and Mike. The Elites summer in the Hamptons, Nick. You're summering in the basement.
entries.this_week: vs Nicholas Kasik: 6-14 with a one-game skid, against 11-9 on a two-game win streak. Cardillo needs a quarterback, a win, and a better name, in that order.
entries.prediction: Kasik wins by 20, and Cardillo calls it a rebuilding year with a straight face.

entries.roast: Here, on the plains of East Lansing, we observe the Nature Boy in his natural habitat: the bottom. For the second straight week he has been chased down and devoured by a larger predator. Last week, 78.75 points. This week, 84.6, the worst beating anybody has taken all season. Watch closely as he makes his fatal mistake. He has Seth McGowan, healthy, rested, ready. Instead, he sends Tyler Allgeier into the open. 1.4 points. McGowan scores 13.7 on the bench. Meanwhile Adonai Mitchell, the prize of his three-way trade, sits in the grass and does nothing at all. And in a final act of survival, today he drops the Ravens defense and adds Tampa Bay's. Remarkable. The animal has lost five in a row and has chosen to rearrange the furniture. Nature is cruel. Taylor's lineup is crueler.
entries.this_week: vs Jacob Maddox: 4-16 and five straight losses, against 16-3-1 on a one-game win streak. The worst record in the league against the best, and the brand-new Bucs defense gets to find out what it signed up for.
entries.prediction: Maddox wins by 50, and Taylor benches whoever would have made it 40.

entries.roast: Welcome, Mr. Hemstreet. Your usual? Mike doesn't order off the menu. He orders whatever the other tables sent back. Thursday he cuts Carson Wentz, Daniel Jones and Deebo Samuel, then picks up Drew Lock and Geno Smith, both dumped by other managers two days earlier, Lock by the Commish and Geno by Drew. Sunday he starts both. Meanwhile Justin Herbert, the quarterback he paid four picks for, sits on the bench with 16.55, right next to Jacoby Brissett's 16.2. And it worked, because Christian McCaffrey scored 50.3 and covered the whole check. That's not a strategy, Mike. That's eating out of the dumpster behind a steakhouse because the chef happens to throw out a filet once a week. Twelve and eight, third-best record in the league, and the power rankings still have him dead last. Even the rankings sent it back.
entries.this_week: vs Drew Hartman: 12-8 on a one-game win streak, against 9-11 and two straight losses. Mike gets Drew, who supplied one of last week's starting quarterbacks for free.
entries.prediction: Mike wins by 15 and starts whatever Drew drops on Tuesday.
